newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares power on before problems halt trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares power on before problems halt trade.

text.p: German shares were inspired by the U.S. to continue their record-breaking run on Wednesday, as an upbeat report from the Fed's Greenspan, a strong close on Wall St and a firm dollar lifted the DAX index in bourse trade.

But a series of technical problems meant that electronic trade was down for periods of the morning before the stock exchange announced that all trade in shares, bonds and derivatives had been suspended due to technical problems.

At the time of the suspension, which was the second time this week that German equities trading has been disrupted by technical difficulties, the DAX index was up 164.57 points, or 3.89 percent, at 4,394.99.
Earlier, the DAX index had briefly managed to breach the 4,400-point barrier for the first time and traders said that before the breakdown the mood on the exchange was almost euphoric.
"The banks are up, the cars are up. The DTB options guys are starting to buy. Everything is good as gold as far as I can see," a Frankfurt trader said.
The dollar trading around 1.83 marks underpinned sentiment.

Other helpful news from the U.S. came in the shape of a speech by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, who said the central bank might have to raise interest rates to head off price pressure, but soothed markets by suggesting this might not happen anytime soon.
Greenspan's comments drove the Dow Jones Industrial index higher as investors interpreted Greenspan's comments as suggesting that Fed policy was on hold. The Dow ended the day up nearly two percent.
Traders said that this gave a valuable boost to the German share market, which has taken its lead from the Dow for many of its moves during the recent bull run.
"The whole Greenspan thing was phenomenally bullish as far as I'm concerned," the broker said.
Bulls prevailed in terms of measuring the outlook for the DAX. One trader said he saw a technical buy signal and said that he saw the DAX hitting 4,500 points in the near term.

Shares in the limelight early on included Deutsche Bank AG, which was up 7.59 percent at 125.50 in mid-session trade percent in pre-bourse trade after it reported better-than-expected results for the first half of 1997.
The group reported a 27.5 percent rise in group net income to 1.5 billion marks in the first half of 1997.
"I think it was bank merger speculation and short-covering which was helping Deutsche early on, more than the figures," a trader said.

Seven out of the ten top gainers in IBIS trade were banks, including Bayerische Vereinsbank up 13.25 marks -- 13.25 percent -- at 113.25 marks and Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel Bank, up 5.60 marks, 7.52 percent, at 80.10 marks.
Both of these banks have been the focus of market attention for the last few days since they announced their intention to merge into one Bavarian super-bank.
